newsitem.title: TURKEY: TURKEY ASKS NEW BIDS TO CHOOSE TELECOM ADVISER.
newsitem.headline: TURKEY ASKS NEW BIDS TO CHOOSE TELECOM ADVISER.

text.p: Turkey has asked six international consortia to submit renewed bids to choose an adviser which will price and run privatisation of its telecommunications company Turk Telekom, a privatisation official said.
"The Privatisation Administration asked the six consortia for their new bids in October. They will submit their bids this month," said the official, who declined to be named.
He said studies to choose an adviser would be completed in the first half of next year.
In late 1995, the OIB had short listed the following six consortia from among 20 groups:
-- Banque Paribas, Kleinwort Benson, Bear Stearns
-- Goldman Sachs, Lazard Freres, UBS, Barclays de Zoete Wedd, Nikko
-- J.P. Morgan, N.M. Rothschild, Merill Lynch
-- Lehman Brothers, Nomura, Deustche Bank, Morgan Grenfell
-- Morgan Stanley, SG Warburg, Citibank, Yamaichi
-- Salomon Brothers, Banque Indosuez Capital, Daiwa, Schroders Plc

The short listed consortia gave their final bids in December 1995, shortly before the tender was cancelled after the constitutional court annulled parts of the previous telecom legislation. Parliament approved a new draft in August to enable the government to privatise Turk Telekom.
Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan's government aimed to raise $3.5 billion through the sale of a minority stake in Turk Telekom.
